run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-17T23:55:34Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend is backed by real frontend error spans: a frontend span error rate of ~0.5/s was measured at 23:55:34Z, and the all-span error series was zero until ~23:52 and returned to zero by ~00:06. Every frontend error in the 23:43-00:10 window sits on the same request path: grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and the /api/data route that calls it (423 failing spans at each level, 1708 frontend error spans total), with frontend-proxy ingress error spans (447.5) mirroring them. The ad service stopped answering exactly when its single-replica Deployment was rolled out: pod template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T23:54:23Z, old pod ad-554b849958-gcmfq killed 23:54:26, new pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz created/started 23:54:23-25. The new ad pod became Ready at 23:54:26 despite having no readiness probe, while its container only logged "Ad service starting." at 23:58:36 and ad's own oteldemo.AdService/GetAds span rate was measured at 0 from 23:59 to ~00:04 before recovering (~0.48/s by 00:06). Latency was not elevated (frontend GetAds 10-minute distribution at 23:59 was essentially the pre-fault 23:49 baseline, nothing above 1s), so the failures were fast connection-level failures, not timeouts. The pod template spec and image (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad) are identical between the old and new ReplicaSets - only the restartedAt annotation differs - so the rollout is the mechanism of the outage, not an identified cause: what issued the restart is not observable because the change_history integration is missing. The only switched-on ad-related flag in the flagd-config ConfigMap (adManualGc) is recorded, but the evidence (no ad error spans, normal ad serving rate before the kill, errors stopping while the flag stays on) argues against it causing this error burst.

claims.text: At 2026-11-17T23:55:34Z the frontend span error rate was 0.5/s for status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR (44.57/s STATUS_CODE_UNSET) on traces_span_metrics_calls_total, so frontend itself was emitting error spans at the time the alert opened.

Frontend's STATUS_CODE_ERROR span rate was 0 at every sampled point from 23:32:34 to 23:52:34, became non-zero from 23:56:34 (1.32/s, rising to 3.30/s at 23:58:34) through 00:04:34, and was 0 again at 00:06:34; UNSET span rate stayed ~42-44/s throughout.

Over 23:43-00:10 the frontend error spans were concentrated on GET (423.2), GET /api/data (423.2), executing api route (pages) /api/data (423.2) and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (423.2), plus tcp.connect (15.2); frontend-proxy showed ingress (447.5) and router frontend egress (423.2) error spans, and frontend total error increase was 1708.1 with frontend-proxy 870.8.

Kubernetes events for otel-demo show Deployment ad scaled replica set ad-d89765fb5 from 0 to 1 at 23:54:23, new pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started 23:54:23-23:54:25, then Deployment ad scaled ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0 and pod ad-554b849958-gcmfq was killed at 23:54:26 (all Normal events).

The new ad ReplicaSet ad-d89765fb5 carries pod template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T23:54:23Z which the previous ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 does not, and its template labels differ only by pod-template-hash.

The pod specs of ad-554b849958 and ad-d89765fb5 are identical: image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, the same env (AD_PORT, FLAGD_HOST, FLAGD_PORT, OTEL_*), the same resource limits (cpu 50m, memory 450Mi), and no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe in either.

Pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz reports condition Ready=True with lastTransitionTime 23:54:26Z, container ad running since 23:54:25Z with restartCount 0 and no lastState, and pod startTime 23:54:23Z - i.e. it was marked Ready immediately although it has no readiness probe.

The only log line retained for container ad in pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz is "Ad service starting." at 2026-11-17T23:58:36.903Z, about four minutes after the container started (23:54:25Z); no previous container instance exists.

The ad service's own oteldemo.AdService/GetAds span rate was 0.73-0.90/s until 23:56:00, dropped to 0.289/s in the window ending 23:58:00, was exactly 0 at the points ending 00:00:00, 00:02:00 and 00:04:00, and recovered to 0.477/s by 00:06:00 - while the frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds error rate was non-zero from the window ending 23:56:00 through 00:03:00 and 0 from 00:04:00.
The ad Service (selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad, port 8080) currently has endpoint 100.96.1.122 backed by pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz, so Service selector/endpoints and pod labels match the new pod.

The flagd-config ConfigMap (demo.flagd.json) currently has adFailure defaultVariant off, adHighCpu off, adManualGc defaultVariant on (variants off=false/on=true, description 'Triggers full manual garbage collections in the ad service'), and cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure all off.

ad's own span status breakdown over 23:43-00:10 shows oteldemo.AdService/GetAds only with STATUS_CODE_UNSET (886.2) and no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series, while its only error increase is 1.01 on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream; fraud-detection shows 2.03 and recommendation 3.04 on their flagd EventStream spans, and accounting/payment show 0 error increase.

Pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-vzsmb (created 23:21:58Z) shows lastState terminated reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, finished 2026-11-17T23:27:18Z, restartCount 1 - about 27 minutes before the frontend error burst began; its error spans in 23:43-00:10 are only 2.03 on a flagd EventStream span.

Most likely mechanism: the 23:54:23 rollout restart of the single-replica Deployment ad removed the only serving ad replica, and because the ad container has no readiness probe the replacement pod was declared Ready at 23:54:26 while its gRPC endpoint was not yet listening (first log 'Ad service starting.' only at 23:58:36, ad GetAds span rate 0 until ~00:03-00:05). Frontend's GetAds calls therefore failed fast for ~9 minutes, producing the frontend error spans on grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and the /api/data route, the frontend-proxy ingress errors, and this alert.

Secondary hypothesis for the size of the outage window: startup of the replacement ad container was unusually slow (container started 23:54:25, first startup log 23:58:36, serving only ~00:03-00:05), which could be caused by its 50m CPU limit or init-time dependency work; the evidence available does not identify which, since only one log line and no container CPU/throttling metrics were available.

Frontend latency was not elevated during the fault, so a timeout/latency cause is not supported: for grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds the 10-minute bucket counts at 23:59 (522 calls, 484 <=100ms, 0 above 1000ms) are essentially the 23:49 baseline (529 calls, 479 <=100ms, 0 above 1000ms), and for GET /api/data only the <=2ms bucket appeared during the fault (131 vs 0 at baseline), which is consistent with immediate connection failures rather than slow responses.

The ad service did not report application errors of its own during the outage window: oteldemo.AdService/GetAds error increase over 23:43-00:10 is absent (only STATUS_CODE_UNSET 886.2), so the failures seen by frontend came from ad being unreachable/not listening rather than from ad returning gRPC errors.

Rejected: that the switched-on adManualGc fault-style flag in the flagd-config ConfigMap caused the frontend error burst. ad served GetAds at 0.73-0.90/s under the same flagd configuration before the pod kill, it produced no ERROR spans, the drop to a measured 0 GetAds rate coincides with the pod kill rather than a flag change, and the frontend errors stopped by ~00:04 while adManualGc is still on.

Follow up on the restart trigger and guard rails: pull audit/change history for the kubectl-style rollout restart recorded in the ad pod template at 2026-11-17T23:54:23Z, add readiness (and startup) probes to the ad container so a not-yet-listening pod is not marked Ready, consider more than one replica for ad to avoid single-replica downtime, and review the ad container's 50m CPU limit as a possible cause of slow startup.

gaps: The actor/reason for the rollout restart recorded as pod template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T23:54:23Z on Deployment ad is unknown: the change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no object or change record showing who applied it was observed.

Why the replacement ad container needed ~4 minutes to log 'Ad service starting.' (23:58:36) and ~9 minutes before ad server spans reappeared is not observable: only one ad log line was retained and no container CPU/throttling metrics were available.

The RequestErrorRate alerting rule could not be inspected: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate and with {severity="warning"} both returned nothing, so the rule expression, threshold and evaluation labels are unknown.

Jaeger returned no frontend traces for 23:53-00:17 and no traces matching error=true or otel.status_code="ERROR", and the ad trace query hit RESULT_TOO_LARGE with the returned sample covering only 23:51:56-23:52:07, so the exact gRPC status code/message of the failing GetAds calls is unknown.
kube-state-metrics series are not present in this Prometheus (get_metric_names {__name__=~"kube_.*"} returned nothing), so deployment available/ready replica timelines for ad are unknown.
Queries for networkpolicies and resourcequotas in otel-demo returned no objects; this only shows the queries matched nothing, so whether such controls existed during the window is unknown.
No frontend container logs were returned for 23:50-00:00, so frontend application log evidence (error text) is unknown.

Error spans for services not returned by the ERROR-increase query (cart, checkout, currency, email, image-provider, product-catalog, quote, shipping, kafka, load-generator) are unknown rather than zero.
next_steps: Obtain audit/change-history for Deployment otel-demo/ad around 2026-11-17T23:54:23Z to identify what issued the rollout restart.
Add readiness/startup probes to the ad container and consider raising its 50m CPU limit or running more than one replica, then verify that a rollout no longer produces a serving gap.
Confirm the RequestErrorRate alert expression and whether it is computed from traces_span_metrics_calls_total status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR, and validate its threshold.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
